title: Plant-based yogurt systems: Mechanistic links from fermentability to quality and bioactivity
abstract: Plant-based yogurt systems are promising dairy alternatives and carriers of plant-derived bioactives, but their quality is difficult to predict because plant matrices differ in fermentable substrates, buffering capacity, protein structure, polysaccharides, lipids, and phytochemicals. This review integrates recent evidence within a composition-process-microstructure-quality-bioactivity framework. It explains how raw materials, starter-matrix compatibility, fermentation behavior, antinutritional factors, protein-polyphenol interactions, and processing-induced structural changes jointly regulate acidification, gel formation, water-holding capacity, texture, sensory quality, digestibility, and functional readouts. It further discusses omics-guided starters, enzyme-assisted modification, artificial intelligence prediction, emerging processing technologies, and microbiota-oriented personalization as tools for matrix-adapted design. Overall, this review proposes a mechanistic route for developing fermented plant foods with improved technological robustness, sensory quality, nutritional functionality, and individualized relevance.

title: Detection of mustard oil adulteration by VOC fingerprinting using a CNT-based electronic nose coupled with LC-MS profiling and supervised learning
abstract: Mustard oil possesses significant nutritional and medicinal value, and its adulteration with cheaper oils poses serious health and economic concerns. This study presents a qualitative, non-destructive approach for detecting mustard oil adulteration using a carbon nanotube (CNT)-based electronic nose (E-nose) integrated with liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) based molecular profiling and supervised machine learning. Volatile organic compound (VOC) profiles of six cold-pressed edible oils (mustard, canola, cottonseed, palm, rice bran and soybean) were characterized using untargeted LC-MS confirming distinct VOC fingerprints. Binary mixtures of adulterated mustard oils (1-80%) were subsequently analyzed using the E-nose. Sensor-derived VOC features were evaluated using unsupervised (PCA, t-SNE) and supervised (LR, LDA, SVM) models. Among the classifiers, SVM achieved the best overall performance with mean classification accuracies of 98.63-99.19% across different adulteration systems. The proposed CNT-based E-nose platform demonstrates strong potential as a rapid, portable and cost-effective screening tool for edible oil authentication and quality assurance.

title: Rapid geographical authentication of Sauce-flavor baijiu using SICRIT-Q-TOF-MS and interpretable machine learning
abstract: Geographical authentication of Sauce-flavor baijiu remains challenging due to its complex composition. A non-targeted metabolomics approach using soft ionization by chemical reaction in transfer coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (SICRIT-Q-TOF-MS) enabled rapid analysis of 134 samples from 10 provinces. 510 ion features were detected, and 202 discriminative features were screened (VIP > 1; FDR-adjusted p 4). Orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) showed internal cross-validated performance (R 2 Y = 0.900, Q 2 = 0.896), with a bootstrap 95% confidence interval of 0.883-0.908 for Q 2 . Fifteen machine-learning algorithms were systematically screened, with Random Forest showing the most balanced internal test-set performance (accuracy = 0.796, AUC = 0.971). A 59-feature model maintained similar performance (accuracy = 0.805, AUC = 0.969). Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) indicated classification was driven by interacting features with nonlinear effects. This study provides an interpretable strategy for geographical origin discrimination of Sauce-flavor baijiu.

title: Aquatic-derived bioactive peptides: molecular mechanisms, digestive fate, and precision nutrition
abstract: Aquatic-derived peptides (ADPs) are bioactive peptides from fish, shellfish, algae, and aquatic by-products. Reported biochemical activities include antioxidant, ACE-inhibitory, and mineral-binding properties, with immunomodulatory and metabolic functions reported. However, an integrated understanding linking peptide structure, bioavailability, and systemic functions remains incomplete. This review summarizes advances from 2020 to 2026 across in silico, in vitro, animal, and human studies, integrating peptidomics, molecular simulations, transport biology, and multi-omics. Particular attention is given to potential pathways through which ADPs may influence the gut-brain, gut-liver, gut-bone, and gut-skin axes. Emerging delivery strategies, including nanoencapsulation, hydrogel-based carriers, and targeted-release systems, are discussed for peptide stability and gastrointestinal delivery. Finally, we summarize challenges in structural standardization, human mechanistic validation, and regulatory considerations, and discuss future directions including AI-assisted peptide design and precision nutrition. Overall, current evidence supports sequence-dependent bioactivity and selected digestive and transport effects, whereas causal multi-organ and individualized responses remain insufficiently validated in humans.

title: A machine learning-assisted colorimetric sensor array based on Fe-doped MnO₂/graphene composites for flavonoid identification and bioactivity prediction in vine tea
abstract: Accurate characterization of flavonoids in vine tea is of considerable importance for assessing its nutritional value and exploring its potential applications in hypoglycemic and hypolipidemic agents. Combining the substrate-responsive catalytic activity of MnFe/GO nanozymes with machine learning-based pattern recognition enabled the rapid and accurate differentiation of three structurally similar flavonoids. Furthermore, a two-stage cascade prediction model was constructed: the first stage employed random forest and gradient boosting regression to predict total concentration and component molar ratios; the second stage used the predicted composition vector as input to a random forest multi-output regression model to predict α-glucosidase and pancreatic lipase inhibitory rates. The results demonstrated good predictive performance and generalization ability. The model demonstrated satisfactory performance in real vine tea samples, enabling simultaneous prediction of flavonoid composition and bioactivity, thereby providing an effective approach for rapid quality assessment of natural products.

title: An integrated strategy to obtain ready-to-use carotenoid extract from persimmon (Diospyros kaki Thunb.) using hydrophobic eutectic solvents: From virtual COSMO-SAC screening to atomistic level mechanism
abstract: Persimmon carotenoids are valuable, but the preparation suffers from the abuse of organic solvents, while the emergence of hydrophobic eutectic solvents (HESs) provides a feasible means to obtain ready-to-use extracts. This study developed an integrated strategy for the preparation and preservation of persimmon carotenoid extract using food-compatible HESs without solvent removal. Profiling identified 42 carotenoids (139.2 μg/g) in persimmon powder, with over 85% existing as esterified forms. Menthol and ethyl hexanoate (molar ratio of 1:1) were selected as the optimal HES via COSMO-SAC high-throughput virtual screening and experimental validation. The dissolution behavior of carotenoids in HESs was regulated by van der Waals interaction and hydrogen-bond anchoring, as evidenced by molecular dynamics simulations. Furthermore, the artificial neural network-genetic algorithm showed alternative potential to response surface methodology in the modeling and optimization of extraction process. The established strategy provides a referenceable means for the rational design and mechanistic analysis of phytochemical extraction.

title: From bioactive chemistry to packaging function: a structure-interaction-release framework for sustainable food packaging
abstract: Bioactive materials offer a promising route to sustainable food packaging with antimicrobial, antioxidant, enzymatic, probiotic, and sensing functions; however, their performance cannot be predicted from intrinsic bioactivity alone. This review establishes a Bioactive-Matrix-Structure-Release-Function (BMSRF) framework linking bioactive chemistry and molecular interactions with matrix architecture, transport behavior, functional efficacy, and food-preservation outcomes. Particular emphasis is placed on the transition from bioactivity to bioavailability and ultimately bioefficacy at the food-packaging interface. Across natural extracts, essential oils, probiotics, enzymes, and nanomaterials, the review identifies interconnected trade-offs among activity, stability, retention, release, mechanical integrity, and barrier performance, interpreting these relationships as design constraints rather than isolated limitations. Based on these relationships, rational design rules are proposed for matching bioactive chemistry, matrix architecture, and release kinetics to food environments and preservation targets. Emerging approaches including advanced encapsulation, stimuli-responsive systems, predictive modeling, and AI-assisted formulation are discussed toward predictive and scalable sustainable packaging design.

title: Integrated abundance analysis and artificial intelligence-assisted screening reveal novel antihypertensive milk-derived tripeptides
abstract: Milk consumption has been associated with reduced blood pressure, yet most studies have focused on a limited number of peptides, such as IPP and VPP. Here, we evaluated the antihypertensive effect of a single serving of milk in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) and developed an integrated computational-experimental framework to identify milk-derived tripeptides with potential bioactivity. Major milk proteins were subjected to in silico gastrointestinal digestion to generate a virtual tripeptide library. Artificial intelligence-assisted structural modeling of angiotensin-converting enzyme-tripeptide interactions, combined with bioinformatic screening and peptide abundance analysis, was used to prioritize candidates with predicted bioactivity and physiological relevance. A total of seven selected tripeptides were further validated by molecular docking and in vivo assays. Several candidates significantly reduced systolic blood pressure in SHRs, with EIV, VAL, and SEE showing effects comparable to IPP. This approach provided an effective strategy for identifying physiologically relevant antihypertensive peptides from complex food proteins.

title: Intelligent De novo Design of Multifunctional Taste Peptides via an integrated deep learning, conditional diffusion, and reinforcement learning platform
abstract: Taste peptides from dietary proteins elicit taste sensations and have reported bioactivities, but their rational prioritization remains hampered by the limited throughput of conventional screening. Here, we describe a multi-stage computational workflow for de novo prioritization of multifunctional taste peptides, combining multi-task benchmarking, conditional diffusion sequence generation, feature-space novelty filtering, and PPO-based sequence optimization. A multi-label dataset of 4801 experimentally reported peptides was assembled from BIOPEP-UWM, MBPDB, FermFooDb, and published taste-peptide benchmark sets. The best-performing classifiers achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values of 0.923 (umami), 0.872 (bitter), 0.828 (ACE-inhibitory), and 0.807 (antioxidant), with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals estimated for each task. Conditional diffusion yielded 9401 unique candidates after validity filtering and deduplication. Novelty-aware filtering and an independently optimized PPO policy were compared using the same composite reward. The novelty score used for ranking is a Euclidean feature-space distance rather than a flow-matching likelihood. All outputs are presented as computational priorities for synthesis and experimental validation, not as measured activities.

title: Artificial intelligence and in silico discovery of senolytic and senescence-associated food peptides
abstract: Cellular senescence, characterized by the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, is a primary driver of age-related tissue dysfunction. While synthetic senolytics have shown promise, concerns regarding systemic toxicity have shifted focus toward sustainable alternatives like food-derived bioactive peptides. This review evaluates AI and in silico methods in senolytic food peptide research, distinguishing discovery, prioritization, and unverified senescence relevance. We evaluate discovery pipelines across soy, dairy, legumes, and marine sources, addressing pharmacokinetics, bioavailability, senescence heterogeneity, gastrointestinal stability, bitterness, and the lack of standardized replicative and therapy-induced experimental senescence models. We further highlight that a substantial proportion of peptides discussed in the current literature are best characterized as senescence-associated candidates that await mechanistic validation, rather than as confirmed senolytics or senomorphics. Future research must prioritize bioengineered 3D human tissue models and long-term clinical validation.

title: Screening and identification of novel walnut-derived hypolipidemic peptides and evaluation of their hypolipidemic effects
abstract: Walnut peptides improve lipid metabolism by alleviating hyperlipidemia-related symptoms and regulating key genes, but their specific high-activity hypolipidemic sequences have not yet been identified, limiting their hypolipidemic potential. In the study, walnut protein hydrolysates were separated by ultrafiltration under optimized enzymatic hydrolysis conditions, and the molecular weight (Mw) < 3 kDa fraction exhibited the highest hypolipidemic potential (pancreatic lipase, PL: 51.35 ± 0.98%; cholesterol esterase, CE: 45.63 ± 1.50%). A hypolipidemic peptide prediction model was constructed using the designed PeptidasGAN model and the random forest (RF) method, and based on this model, three highly active hypolipidemic peptides (VLTL, LFL, and LVV) were screened and identified from the fraction with MW < 3 kDa. In vitro experimental results showed that these three peptides exhibited strong inhibitory activity against the key targets of hyperlipidemia, PL and CE, with IC₅₀ values of approximately 0.027 mg/mL and 0.070 mg/mL, respectively, comparable to those of the positive control. Molecular interaction and molecular dynamics simulation results indicated that the peptide-target complexes adopted stable conformations, and free energy analysis further demonstrated a clear energetic advantage. In addition, 3T3-L1 cell experiments showed that these peptides significantly improved lipid accumulation and lipid-related parameters (TC, TG, LDL-C, and HDL-C), thereby confirming their potential hypolipidemic activity. Overall, the three walnut-derived hypolipidemic peptides identified in this study exhibited effective hypolipidemic activity.

title: Integrated multi-omics and machine learning analysis of 3-phenyllactic acid variation across diverse kimchi types
abstract: 3-Phenyllactic acid (PLA) is a bioactive metabolite in kimchi with antifungal activity. We investigated PLA formation across kimchi types using targeted metabolomics and bacterial community profiling, including lactic acid bacteria (LAB) composition. Baechu, chonggak, and radish kimchi showed high PLA levels, whereas mustard and godeulppaegi showed lower levels associated with precursor imbalance. Watery kimchi types, including dongchimi and nabak, showed low PLA levels, likely due to high water content. Multivariate analysis based on metabolite profiles and microbial composition classified samples into four groups reflecting PLA levels, precursor balance, and ingredient origin. Random Forest and XGB classified the four groups with out-of-fold accuracies of 0.994 and 0.929, respectively, while comparisons with simpler linear and kernel-based models supported the robustness of predictive patterns. Integrated analysis indicated that PLA accumulation was associated with precursor availability, ingredient matrix, and LAB composition, providing an integrated assessment of factors associated with PLA distribution among kimchi types.

title: Ultrasound-assisted enzymatic synthesis of medium- and long-chain triacylglycerols from tricaprylin and algal oil
abstract: Medium and long-chain triacylglycerols (MLCTs) are functional lipids, but their efficient synthesis in various systems remains challenging. An ultrasound-assisted enzymatic interesterification process was developed using tricaprylin and algal oil as substrates. The optimized enzymatic conditions were obtained by artificial neural network modeling. The structure of enzyme and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) of enzymatic process were both evaluated. The results showed that the MLCT yield reached 69.16%, with Cy-Cy-DHA as the predominant product (28.99%). Only slight structural changes were observed in the enzyme after ultrasound treatment, while the apparent reaction rate constant increased by nearly 2.8-fold and the activation energy decreased. CFD showed that ultrasound improved substrate diffusion and mixing with a lower maximum static pressure than stirring (178 vs. 259 Pa), suggesting MLCT synthesis was enhanced mainly by mass transfer intensification. This study provides valuable insights into mechanisms underlying ultrasound-enhanced enzymatic processes and guides their further scale-up and industrial application.

title: An interpretable CNN–grad-CAM framework for detection and quantification of cow milk adulteration in goat milk using excitation–emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopy.
abstract: Cow milk adulteration in goat milk is difficult to detect because of subtle compositional differences. A rapid, non-destructive method combining excitation-emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectroscopy with a convolutional neural network (CNN) was developed for the detection and quantification of cow milk adulteration. The CNN directly processed raw EEM matrices as image-like inputs without prior fluorescence decomposition. For binary classification, it achieved 98.65% accuracy, with precision, recall, specificity, and F1-score exceeding 98%, whereas it outperformed SVM in seven-class classification. For quantitative prediction, CNN yielded marginally better results than SVR, with an RMSEP of 4.84% and an R P 2 of 0.91, compared with 4.88% and 0.90 for SVR, respectively. Grad-CAM and PARAFAC showed partial overlap between CNN-discriminative and protein-related regions, indicating that protein signals contributed to, but did not solely determine, the model decisions. This EEM-CNN framework enables rapid, interpretable screening of cow milk adulteration in goat milk under controlled conditions.

title: Molecular mechanism of SIRT1 activation by polymethoxyflavonoids derived from citrus peels
abstract: Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) activation by small molecules is linked to aging-related health benefits. We investigated how citrus peel–derived polymethoxyflavonoids (PMFs), 3,5,6,7,8,3′,4′-heptamethoxyflavone (HMF) and 5,6,7,8,3′,4′-hexamethoxyflavone (nobiletin), activate SIRT1. Both compounds modestly but reproducibly increased deacetylase activity toward acetylated p53 and PGC-1α peptides. HMF and nobiletin significantly increased catalytic efficiency ( k cat / K m ) toward both substrates, whereas K m decreased significantly only for the PGC-1α peptide. Residue-resolved NMR analyses localized the PMF-responsive surface to the α2–loop–α3 region of the SIRT1 N-terminal domain (NTD), with overlapping perturbations at T209, E214, L220, I223, and V224. Tryptophan fluorescence-quenching measurements provided complementary evidence. Docking and molecular-dynamics simulations showed that both PMFs remained on this NTD surface while adopting multiple binding modes. Integrative models combining AlphaFold 3–derived SIRT1–substrate complexes with MD-derived PMF poses suggest that NTD-bound PMFs may stabilize a catalytically favorable SIRT1–substrate state, providing molecular insight into SIRT1 activation by citrus-derived PMFs.

title: Rapid and accurate PLS-RBF neural networks for multi-constituent prediction in intact fresh maize kernels using NIR spectroscopy
abstract: Developing robust and accurate near-infrared (NIR) neural network calibration models for intact fresh maize kernels remains challenging in fresh maize breeding. In this study, four rapid and reliable PLS-RBF neural networks were established by integrating PLS feature extraction with ridge-regression-optimized RBF neural networks, to predict the contents of amylopectin, protein, crude fiber, and total sugar in intact fresh maize kernels, respectively. Compared with PCA-based models, PLS-based models consistently exhibited superior predictive performance, with RPD improvements of at least 15.89%,72.85%,54.77% and 19.01% for amylopectin, protein, crude fiber, and total sugar, respectively. The optimized PLS-RBF neural networks presented acceptable predictive performance, with R P 2 value ranging from 0.871 to 0.970 and RPD values between 2.799 and 5.836. Overall, the proposed PLS-RBF neural networks provide efficient, nondestructive approaches for multi-constituent assessment of intact fresh maize kernels and demonstrate considerable potential for practical quality control applications within the collected sample population.

title: Matrix-specific design of food-grade probiotic microcapsules: Wall materials, scalable processing, and AI-enabled optimization
abstract: Microencapsulation of probiotics has been widely studied to improve microbial viability during processing and storage, but its performance in real food systems remains inconsistent because protection, controlled release, sensory acceptability, and manufacturing feasibility must be balanced simultaneously. This review examines key encapsulation techniques by linking microstructural characteristics with practical scale-up constraints. It also discusses wall materials, including polysaccharides, proteins, and prebiotic matrices, with emphasis on their interactions governing encapsulation capacity, swelling behavior, and storage stability. The review further analyzes food matrix adaptability by relating the characteristics and constraints of different food systems to probiotic protection and microcapsule performance and highlights an AI-driven optimization framework that integrates material characteristics, process parameters, food-matrix constraints, and probiotic performance within multivariable and multi-objective design. Future progress requires matrix-specific wall materials and preparation methods, regulatory compliance, scalable manufacturing, and AI-assisted optimization, thereby supporting the transition of probiotic microcapsules from laboratory prototypes to industrial production.

title: Intelligent packaging for tofu preservation: a comprehensive review of advanced materials and pathways toward integrated AI-driven systems
abstract: Tofu, a highly perishable and increasingly popular global staple, has received limited research attention regarding intelligent packaging. This review systematically consolidates recent advances, spanning molecular spoilage mechanisms to prospective integrated AI-driven systems. It analyzes two main pillars: advanced materials-evolving from controlled-release to stimuli-responsive systems-highlighting development directions for tofu-specific smart packaging; and sensing technologies-including visual indicators and embedded sensors-documenting failure modes and matrix interference. The discussion culminates in a conceptual framework for AI-enabled systems, noting that no fully integrated implementation currently exists for tofu. It identifies integration gaps, hardware constraints, and the absence of tofu-specific datasets. Additionally, IoT and blockchain technologies are evaluated for connectivity and trust throughout the supply chain. Finally, key commercialization challenges-technical, economic, regulatory, and environmental-are synthesized, and a co-design research agenda is proposed. This work provides a roadmap for next-generation intelligent packaging to enhance shelf life, safety, and supply chain efficiency for tofu and other perishable foods.

title: A robust nanobody-magnetic bead immunoassay for food safety monitoring: Sensitive detection of viral contamination in giant salamander
abstract: The Chinese giant salamander is a valued food source of high-quality protein; however, the prevalence of Giant Salamander Iridovirus (GSIV) poses a significant threat to the safety and stability of the aquaculture food supply chain. Rapid and sensitive screening of viral pathogens in complex food matrices is therefore critical. We developed a bridge-free double-nanobody sandwich ELISA using magnetic beads (MBs) for detection of GSIV. AlphaFold 3 modeling suggested that covalent immobilization via conserved framework lysines may promote an optimal "upright" nanobody orientation, significantly enhancing capture efficiency compared with passive adsorption. The assay achieved a detection limit of 2.2 × 10 5 PFU/mL within 2 h, with sensitivity comparable to that of our previously reported pAb-based assay. The method exhibited exceptional resistance to matrix interference in undiluted tissue homogenates and was adapted to a semi-automated workflow. This work provides a scalable foundation for automated pathogen surveillance in aquatic food supply chains, ensuring food safety.

title: Comprehensive evaluation of the nutritional composition of Atlantic chub mackerel (Scomber colias): Influence of cooking methods
abstract: Nutritional composition and the impact of boiling and grilling on nutrient stability of the Atlantic chub mackerel (Scomber colias) were evaluated. Raw fish showed high protein content (22 g/100 g), a profile rich in omega-3 fatty acids (30%), and exceptional vitamin B 12 levels (28 μg/100 g). Thermal processing led to moisture loss, resulting in apparent increases in nutrient concentrations. However, True Retention Values (TRVs) demonstrated that these changes were primarily driven by concentration effects rather than net nutrient synthesis. High retention was observed for proteins (86-89%), lipids (72-80%), essential amino acids (86-102%), and vitamin B 12 (92-105%), indicating limited losses. Lipid quality indices (AI = 0.58-0.62; TI ≈ 0.27) and protein quality further supported the nutritional excellence of this species. Overall, boiling and grilling preserved the key attributes of S. colias, confirming its relevance as a sustainable and nutrient-dense seafood resource.

title: Competitive difference-driven Ag@Pt nanozyme on a single gold nanowire sensing platform integrated with machine learning for accurate identification of multiple tetracycline antibiotics
abstract: The wide use of tetracycline antibiotics (TCs) exists serious public safety concern for human health due to their accumulation in foods and environments. Meanwhile, various kinds of TCs are frequently present simultaneously in practical environments, it is vital to come up with innovative solutions for high-sensitivity detection and accurate identification. Herein, a novel strategy of competitive difference-driven Ag@Pt nanozyme on a single gold nanowire (Au NW) sensing platform was developed for accurate identification of multiple TCs. Hollow dendritic Ag@Pt nanoparticles (NPs) with peroxidase-like (POD-like) activity have been synthesized and can decompose H 2 O 2 to produce reactive oxygen species (ROS), which subsequently oxidize 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) into oxidized TMB (ox-TMB). In the presence of both TCs and TMB, a competitive reaction with ROS occurs, attenuating the extent of TMB oxidation. Building on this, this platform integrates surface-enhanced Raman scattering and electrochemical (SERS/EC) techniques and further combines them with machine learning to achieve ultrasensitive quantitative detection and accurate identification of five TCs, including minocycline (MC), tetracycline (TET), oxytetracycline (OTC), chlortetracycline (CTC), and doxycycline (DOX). It enables accurate detection of various targets at low concentrations ranging from 2 × 10 -5 ppm to 2 × 10 -2 ppm, with a detection limit as low as 3.54 × 10 -7 ppm for MC. This study combines efficient catalytic activity of nanozymes, the significant advantages brought by the miniaturization of the single Au NW platform, and the structural differences among various TCs, offering significant application value for the rapid, direct, and simultaneous detection of multiple hazards in the environment and food chain.

title: Dual-mode detection of tetracyclines in animal-derived food samples based on MOF-on-MOF heterostructure fluorescent sensor coupled with machine learning algorithms
abstract: Tetracyclines (TCs) that accumulate in food enter the human body through the food chain, leading to drug resistance and health risks. This study synthesized a heterostructure fluorescent sensor, Zn-TCPP-MOF/NH 2 -MIL-53(Al) (abbreviated ZTA) for TCs detection. A dual-mode detection system was established by integrating fluorescence spectroscopy with machine learning algorithms and fluorescence imaging with YOLOv5, enabling precise detection of TCs. The π-π stacking reduced ZTA electron density to promote electron transfer, inducing specific recognition of TCs with a low detection limit of 0.012 μmol/L. Machine learning algorithms of k-means clustering, hierarchical cluster analysis, support vector machine, random forest, logistic regression, and decision tree achieved 100.0%, and YOLOv5 reached 99.8% precision for TCs identification. The ZTA sensor achieved recovery rates between 95.40%-108.50% for TCs detection in animal-derived foods. This study facilitated the design of a MOF-on-MOF heterostructure sensor and provided an intelligent detection strategy for the rapid on-site monitoring of antibiotic residues.

title: Deep chemometrics for retrospective auditing of the water-nutrient nexus in olive oil via 1D-CNN and explainable AI
abstract: Transitioning toward high-value functional food markets increases demand for forensic tools capable of verifying the "water-nutrient nexus", the complex agronomic interplay between irrigation and fertilization that shapes olive oil composition and authenticity. Conventional chemometrics often fail to capture synergistic, non-linear cultivation fingerprints within complex chemical matrices. This study introduces a "Deep Chemometrics" framework for retrospective auditing of olive oil history using FTIR spectroscopy and a customized one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN). The framework was developed from 324 FTIR spectra representing nine irrigation × fertilization (W × F) regimes and incorporated physics-informed data augmentation to overcome limited sample availability. The optimized 1D-CNN achieved 97.89% validation accuracy (validation loss = 0.0548) and 83% accuracy on a held-out test set (macro-averaged precision = 0.85, recall = 0.83, F1-score = 0.83), representing a 25.8% improvement over the baseline model. Gradient-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) consistently identified the ester carbonyl stretching vibration (1744 cm -1 ) and CH₂ asymmetric stretching vibration (2922 cm -1 ) as the principal spectral features driving classification. Representative constrained pseudo-Voigt peak deconvolution, together with non-parametric (Kruskal-Wallis) statistical analysis, confirmed significant treatment-dependent differences within these diagnostic bands (1744 cm -1 : p = 0.0076; 2922 cm -1 : p = 0.0025), providing independent spectroscopic validation of the CNN-derived feature importance. By integrating deep learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and spectroscopic validation, the proposed framework provides a transparent, scientifically interpretable, and robust strategy for retrospective authentication of olive oils according to their irrigation and fertilization history, thereby strengthening agricultural transparency and supporting supply-chain authenticity.

title: Enzymatic detoxification mechanisms of histamine in fish and fermented aquatic products: research progress and future development strategies
abstract: Histamine is a biogenic amine and a chemical food safety hazard in fish and fermented aquatic products. Prevention and enzymatic degradation are complementary strategies. This review compares the catalytic mechanisms of diamine oxidase, histamine dehydrogenase, multicopper oxidase and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, the latter as a moonlighting enzyme with limited histamine-degrading activity. Building on these mechanisms, we evaluate kinetic limitations from high salinity, low pH, and competing amines in fish and fermented aquatic products, including fish sauce and canned tuna homogenates, although final-product validation remains lacking. Food-grade immobilization and whole-cell biocatalysis are discussed as current or applied approaches, while AI-guided protein design and micro-/nanomotor systems remain at proof-of-concept or early-development stages. Despite progress in understanding histamine-degrading enzymes, application remains hindered by short enzymatic half-lives, process incompatibility, and inhibitor vulnerability. We propose a conceptual multi-hurdle framework centered on enzymatic degradation and complementary supply-chain measures, shifting seafood safety from reactive monitoring toward proactive control.

title: The threat of climate change to anthocyanin content in black wolfberry fruit
abstract: Climate associations with wild-fruit quality remain incompletely quantified. This study assessed climate-anthocyanin associations in black wolfberry (Lycium ruthenicum) and projected changes. Anthocyanins in 200 samples collected across seven regions in 2017 were quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography and modeled using random forest. Regional differences were significant (P 2 = 0.84; mean temperature of the warmest quarter had the highest predictive importance (percentage increase in mean squared error, 44%). This pattern, high contents in Qaidam and Hexi but low contents in Turpan, persisted during 2005-2020. Under Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 5-8.5, conditional projections indicated a 30% decline in the Qaidam Basin during 2081-2100. These findings suggest that warming may threaten black wolfberry quality and underscore the need for climate-adaptive cultivation strategies.

title: Decoding jujube aroma: Integrated extraction, advanced analytical strategies, formation mechanisms, influencing factors, and future perspectives
abstract: Jujube is a characteristic fruit of China with distinctive aroma and high nutritional value. This review summarizes advances in the extraction and analysis of free and glycosidically bound volatile organic compounds (VOCs), odor-active compounds, aroma formation mechanisms, and influencing factors. More than 300 VOCs have been identified, including esters, ketones, aldehydes, acids, and pyrazines. Esters, particularly ethyl decanoate, are important contributors to fruity aroma and are formed through alcohol and fatty acid metabolism, followed by acyl-CoA formation and alcohol acyltransferase (AAT)-catalyzed esterification. The lipoxygenase-hydroperoxide lyase-alcohol dehydrogenase pathway and β-oxidation also contribute to precursor supply. Multi-omics and enzymology facilitate the identification of key genes, enzymes, and pathways. Emerging approaches, including stable isotope tracing, molecular docking, machine learning, neuroimaging, and olfactory cell-based biosensors, offer new opportunities to elucidate aroma formation and perception and enable aroma prediction and quality control. This review provides insights into jujube aroma formation and quality improvement.

title: Quantitative prediction of freshness of fish muscle tissue by machine learning coupled with MALDI-TOF MS
abstract: This study developed a prediction model for freshness analysis of fish muscle tissue based on MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry (MS) combined with machine learning (ML) algorithms. Dorsal muscle samples of large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) stored at 4 °C for different periods were analyzed as models. The sensory quality of the samples was evaluated at 0, 1, 3, 5, and 7 days of storage using a 10-point scale. Sensory evaluation results show that the overall acceptability scores decreased from 9.8 at day 0 to 3.3 at day 7 during refrigerated storage, falling below the acceptance threshold (5.0) between day 3 and 5. The mass spectral data of protein extracts of dorsal fish muscle samples were obtained by MALDI-TOF MS. Six ML models were constructed based on 315 mass spectra, and compared. The XGBoost model shows the superior performance for predicting the freshness of large yellow croaker fish dorsal muscle tissue, with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.978, and residual predictive deviation (RPD) of 6.742. An 8:2 train/test split of mass spectral data is appropriate for constructing the models. The impact of data partitioning on the models' performance was evaluated using a leave-one-fish-out cross-validation (LOFO). XGBoost remains the optimal performing model (R 2 = 0.905 ± 0.074) under LOFO. A model performance ranking keeps consistent with that under the 8:2 split. SHAP analysis, combined with tryptic digestion and peptide mass fingerprinting searching, identified four proteins that can serve as potential biomarkers for monitoring freshness change during storage of the analyzed fish muscle tissue. During the single-blind validation using commercial samples, 29 predictions among the 30 analyzed samples remain within the model's error tolerance of 0.5 d, with an overall prediction accuracy of 96.67% (n = 30). It provides a valuable methodological reference for the laboratory-based quality assessment of aquatic products.

title: Antioxidant mechanisms of polyphenols in the storage and preservation of marine foods: a comprehensive review
abstract: Marine foods deteriorate during frozen storage, driven by protein and lipid oxidation and manifesting as colour browning, texture softening, and flavour loss. Polyphenols, multi-target natural antioxidants, offer considerable potential for preservation. The review summarises deterioration patterns, emphasising oxidation mechanisms, evaluates current preservation technologies, and examines advances in polyphenol application. Polyphenols act via radical scavenging, metal chelation, enzyme modulation, and target protein protection, and exert synergistic effects when combined with packaging or physical methods. However, polyphenol application remains constrained by inadequate stability, fragmented data, and unclear structure-activity relationships. Future priorities include stabilised polyphenol release via encapsulation or grafting, AI-driven construction of standardised datasets, and machine learning-based elucidation of preservation patterns to enable intelligent prediction and targeted formulation optimisation.

title: Melatonin regulates protein structures of wheat under shading for cookie crack ratio and digestibility modifications
abstract: The crack ratio and nutritional value of cookies depend on wheat protein structures, yet how melatonin modifies these attributes under shading remains unclear. This study evaluated the effects of melatonin (200 μmol L -1 ) on protein structure and cookie-making quality in shaded wheat. Under shading, melatonin increased glutenin, gliadin, total protein, and small polymeric protein content, and raised β-sheet and α-helix proportions by up to 14.4% and 13.2%, respectively, strengthening non-covalent interactions into a more cross-linked gluten network. Melatonin also elevated sulfur-containing and aromatic amino acids, improving nutritional value and digestibility. A SegFormer-based machine learning model showed melatonin reduced the cookie crack ratio by 18.8-30.7% and improved homogeneity. Protein content, γ-gliadin, and small polymeric proteins governed the crack ratio, whereas digestibility was primarily associated with small polymeric proteins. Collectively, melatonin regulates crack ratio and digestibility by modulating amino acid profiles and protein structures, offering a promising approach to enhance cookie-making quality.

title: Ligand-based prediction of novel sweetener candidates
abstract: Artificial sweeteners raise health concerns due to disrupted appetite regulation and potential cardiometabolic risks. Discovering novel, high-intensity, low-calorie sweeteners remains a significant challenge. In this study, we present a robust ligand-based machine learning framework using our in-house Iterative Stochastic Elimination (ISE) algorithm to distinguish between sweet and bitter compounds. By screening three vast chemical libraries; Enamine HTS, Enamine REAL, and ZINC Druglike, we identified a diverse set of potential sweeteners. Our models showed high accuracy and specificity, minimizing false positives and maximizing enrichment of true actives. To refine these hits, we integrated molecular docking targeting the T1R2 Venus flytrap domain and filtered for PAINS/BRENK liabilities, resulting in a prioritized set of 92 candidate molecules. Tanimoto similarity analysis confirmed that the majority of these hits represent novel chemotypes, distinct from known modulators. This workflow demonstrates the power of combining physico-chemical-based models with structural filtration to accelerate the discovery of novel sweeteners.

title: Early-warning evaluation of pasteurized milk spoilage during storage and distribution
abstract: Hidden temperature deviations within the cold chain are a major contributor to global food waste, yet existing quality assurance methods predominantly rely on lagging indicators that fail to capture early-stage spoilage. Here, we integrate high-resolution foodomics with machine learning approaches to identify a biomarker for pasteurized milk freshness: N-((4-amino-2-methylpyrimidin-5-yl)methyl)formamide (AMF). Through structural elucidation and isotope tracing, we revealed that AMF is formed via a specific hydrolytic ring-opening pathway of thiamine. Importantly, perturbation experiments using sterile UHT milk, NaOH, and formic acid further suggested that alkaline microenvironments and spoilage-associated biochemical activity may facilitate this transformation. Validated on datasets from diverse geographic regions and processing methods, we established a quantitative spoilage warning threshold at 1.7 ng/mL, and the early-warning sensitivity allows detection of transient high-temperature exposures as brief as 6 h. This promising molecular indicator enables a shift in milk quality control from retrospective rejection to prospective prevention, acting as an indicator of thermal history and allowing precise, early detection of temperature abuse in complex dairy supply chains.

Machine learning-enabled discrimination and key feature identification of functional whey protein ingredients based on multidimensional compositional, physicochemical, and structural properties
abstract: Commercial functional whey protein ingredients are highly heterogeneous, making reliable classification challenging. In this study, 16 commercial whey protein ingredients, including microparticulated (MWP), thermostable (TWP), and gel-forming whey proteins (GWP), were characterized using 41 compositional, physicochemical, functional and structural variables. Eleven machine-learning algorithms were evaluated using repeated nested group-based cross-validation. XGBoost showed the strongest overall performance, achieving a mean accuracy of ~0.972 and a macro-F1 score of ~0.970, while permutation testing supporting above-chance discrimination (p = 0.001). Feature-importance and SHAP analyses consistently identified β-lactoglobulin, α-lactalbumin and secondary-structure-related variables as important contributors to classification. XGBoost retained high classification performance when only four features were retained within each outer training fold, suggesting that fewer measurements could suffice for preliminary classification. Although larger sample sets and further external validation are required before industrial application, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of identifying multivariate signatures associated with predefined functional whey protein classes.

title: Identification of potential regulators of caffeine biosynthesis in shading- and nano‑selenium–treated tea leaves based on integrated bioinformatics and AlphaFold3 analysis
abstract: Caffeine is an important flavor and bioactive compound in tea, yet external stimuli-induced regulatory networks of caffeine biosynthesis remain largely unclear. Our study showed that shading and nano‑selenium (SeNPs) treatments respectively increased caffeine content in tea leaves from 35.96 mg/g to approximately 43 mg/g, whereas their combined treatment exerted a synergistic effect, raising it to 51.12 mg/g. Correlation of transcriptome with caffeine content and treatment factors via WGCNA and Mantel tests identified 4 key gene modules and 64 transcription factors (TFs). To accelerate TF screening, we established a rapid and high-throughput screening strategy by integrating AlphaFold3 with JASPAR motif prediction, resulting in 10 candidate TF-DNA complexes. Subsequent validation in yeast and tobacco systems confirmed that CsTSO1 directly binds to the promoter of CsSAMS. Our study uncovers how shading and SeNPs modulate caffeine biosynthesis in tea plants, and provide an AI-assisted framework for efficient TF screening in plant metabolic network.
